newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian police search election monitors' offices.
newsitem.headline: Zambian police search election monitors' offices.

text.p: Zambian police on Monday raided the offices of two election watchdog groups that criticised last week's polls in which President Frederick Chiluba won a landslide re-election.

The groups rejected the results of presidential and parliamentary elections which returned Chiluba to power for a second term with his only serious opponent, Kenneth Kaunda, barred from standing by a new law.
Witnesses said police seized documents from the offices of the umbrella Committee for a Clean Campaign (CCC) before searching the offices of the Zambia Independent Monitoring Team.
The raids followed the release on Sunday night of the groups' leaders, arrested earlier in the day.
Ngande Mwanajiti, of the CCC group of 19 non-governmental and civic groups which monitored the ballot, and ZIMT's Alfred Zulu were picked up by police for questioning on Sunday morning.
Lawyers present during the search of the CCC offices accused Chiluba's government of trying to silence criticism of the elections, marred by poor turnout and an opposition boycott.
"The searches are nothing but legalised break-ins," CCC lawyer Sakwiba Sikota told Reuters.
His group was one of several that accused the government of abusing state resources and using state media to tilt in the favour of Chiluba's ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy.
Local and foreign election observers said the actual voting last Monday was mostly in order.

"Father of the Nation" Kaunda was excluded from challenging for the presidency by law and most opposition parties called on supporters to stay away in a protest. They have also threatened to continue a campaign of civil disobedience.
Police gave no comment on the detentions or searches.

Half of Zambia's 4.6 million eligible voters were excluded from the rolls because of flawed registration, but Chiluba rejected opposition criticism and took his oath of office for a second term on Thursday.
He has placed security forces on alert for political unrest.
